sources.title: VENTURE experiment result: structural release-contract flags in 400 fresh npm packages (frequency)
sources.excerpt: Packages with at least one structural flag: 49 (12.3%), in 42 package families. … Flagged release pairs: 68 (0.6% of pairs).
sources.limitations: Own experiment. Rules applied to registry metadata only.

sources.title: VENTURE experiment: manual audit of 20 structural flags (one per package family)
sources.excerpt: Genuine: 13 of 20 (65%). Debatable: 5. Not genuine: 2. … Of the 13 genuine flags, 5 (#5, #8, #10, #14, #20) are genuine only because an added exports map blocks deep imports of files the package shipped but did not document.
sources.limitations: Judged by a research session against the first audit's criteria. One reviewer, small sample.

sources.title: VENTURE experiment: exploratory analysis of which structural rules are precise
sources.excerpt: two independent samples now agree that a small set of removal rules is precise (13 of 13 audited flags genuine). But it fires for only about 1 in 20 popular packages over two years.
sources.limitations: Exploratory, post hoc. Small per-rule counts.

evidence.claim: On 400 fresh popular npm packages, structural rules alone flagged at least one minor or patch release in 12.3% of packages over two years.
evidence.quote: Packages with at least one structural flag: 49 (12.3%), in 42 package families.

evidence.claim: Only 13 of 20 audited structural flags were genuine (65%), short of the 70% bar. Five of the 13 depend on counting blocked deep imports of undocumented files; without them it's 8 of 20.

Removal rules (export path removed, CLI command removed, a peer's minimum major raised) were genuine in all 13 audited cases across both samples, but fire for only about 1 in 20 popular packages over two years.
evidence.quote: two independent samples now agree that a small set of removal rules is precise (13 of 13 audited flags genuine)
evidence.context: Exploratory, post hoc. Small per-rule counts.

evidence.claim: Maintainers of a popular ESLint plugin confirmed shipping a breaking change in a minor release by accident: they deprecated 5.4.0 after releasing 6.0.0 the same day.
